1 mountains  2 valleys  3 forests  4 music  5 morning  6 evening

and the 12 six-line stanzas are the normal sestina rotation

1 2 3 4 5 6
6 1 5 2 4 3
3 6 4 1 5 2
2 3 6 4 1 5
5 4 1 3 6 2
4 5 2 6 3 1
etc.

so that stanzas 1-12 are all in form.  The tornada is lines 73-75.

In the text as printed the tornada is

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;   1,2
74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music            4
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.         5,6

so that 3 forests is missing from the envoi and 4 music is alone in
line 74.  The only line of the body which ends in music and which
contains forests in the middle is

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;

25 ends in music like 74, so interchanging 25 with 74 leaves every
stanza end-word unchanged and puts the six end-words into the
tornada in the normal 1-2 / 3-4 / 5-6 disposition

73 mountains … valleys
74 forests … music
75 morning … evening

i.e. the usual sestina envoi.  The misplaced pair is therefore line 25
with line 74.
